description: BROWSE: list many matching objects, filtered by keyword, category, group, kind or release year, with paging. Use it when the user wants options or a list ('which M3 screws are there', 'all NEMA motors', '2023 phones', 'free files in Fasteners'), or to find a slug when the name is vague. Not for one object's numbers: for a named object call get_part_dimensions_bolt_pattern_cad instead (one call returns its full sheet, fits and files). Returns summaries (overall size, file count, URL), with key dimensions inline for the top three. Matching: every query word must appear in the object's name, aliases, tags, category or group, case-insensitive ('80-40', '80 x 40' and '8040' alike); filters combine with AND. An empty result is not an error: retry with fewer words, or file request_object. Read-only against the published catalog snapshot; no auth, no charge.

group.description: Exact group name within the category, from list_categories.

kind.description: modern/vintage: a product; standard: a part defined by a published standard; hardware: a generated part with free files.

les_only.description: Only parts used in Long Earth Society builds.

offset.description: Start index; pass next_offset from the previous page.

query.description: Keywords; omit to list by filters alone.

year.description: Release year for products: '2023', '2020s' or '2010-2019'. Objects with no year are excluded when set.

name: find_geometry

next.description: What to call next: get_geometry for a full sheet, or a hint when nothing matched.

next_offset.description: Offset to pass for the next page, or null on the last page.

free_files.description: How many free STEP/STL files the object has (0 = dimension sheet only).

overall_mm.description: Overall size in mm: length, width, height (diameter for round parts); null where unpublished.

slug.description: Object slug: pass it to get_geometry, get_fits, get_free_files or get_file_content.

offset.description: Index of the first summary in this page.

title: Browse and filter the catalog (lists of matching objects)
